title: Debunking the Dirty Dozen (w/ Food Science Babe, food scientist) - Get Real Health
summary: A food scientist argues the Dirty Dozen ignores dose, organic farms use pesticides too, and conventional residues are far below safety limits.

assertions.quote: organic pesticides exist right organic doesn't mean no pesticides
in terms of safety and toxicity uh they're going to have overlapping toxicities
99 plus percent of what they test is the the pesticides that they detect are well below the tolerance levels
it's really not an evidence-based list because not only are they not taking the dose into account
eat your fruits and vegetables and don't don't worry about organic don't worry about conventional
the usda pdp doesn't actually test for most of the pesticides used in organic farming

verdicts.note: The Pesticide Data Program tests hundreds of compounds including some used in organic, but it does not measure substances such as copper and sulfur.

assertions.quote: it impacts specifically low-income shoppers and they end up buying less produce overall
a lot of them really haven't been as rigorously tested as some of these synthetic ones

verdicts.note: Some older natural pesticides were grandfathered with thinner data packages, but EPA still has to register them and many are low-risk biopesticides.
In the EU, pesticides approved for organic use are evaluated under the same legal framework and toxicological testing as other pesticides; EU-specific.

assertions.quote: organic farming is actually allowed to have um conventional pesticides but it has to be under like one percent or something

verdicts.note: USDA rules let organic food keep its status if residues of prohibited pesticides stay under 5 percent of the EPA tolerance.

7 CFR 205.671 excludes a product from organic sale only when residue testing finds prohibited substances above 5 percent of the EPA tolerance, so residues below that fraction do not by themselves cost the organic label.
